artifacts.notes: Project Gutenberg eBook 29765, wrapper included. Extent as measured by the retrieving lane: complete Project Gutenberg text of Webster's Unabridged Dictionary (1913); negative for an "inner man" headword, one incidental quotation only. ACCESS LIMITATION, AND IT IS A SIZE ARGUMENT MEASURED IN BYTES: 28,956,350 bytes, five times the largest artifact this repository retains, for a file registered only to carry one bounded negative -- the retrieving lane found no "inner man" headword in it and one incidental quotation. A reader without the network cannot open the dictionary from a checkout; the negative can be replayed by re-fetching this exact URL and this digest, and it is bounded by this transcription of the 1913 printing and by nothing wider.
artifacts.rights_basis: Two things have to be separated. Project Gutenberg's permission page states that the vast majority of its eBooks are in the public domain in the United States and that nobody can grant or withhold permission to use them -- but that is a statement about the book, not about the file. This file is wrapped in Project Gutenberg's licence header and footer, which carry the Project Gutenberg trademark and conditions on its use. The wrapper-bearing bytes are therefore recorded as the hashed derivation input and are not retained in Git; what is retained is the derivative named in `notes`, from which the wrapper has been removed, leaving only the text whose rights the permission page settles. Here the derivative does not exist, so the rights position is recorded and nothing is retained; the reason is size and is stated in `notes`.
